stem:
Harare Packaging Ltd buys the business of the partnership Tanaka and Moyo on 1 April 2026. The partners share profits and losses 3 : 2. The assets and liabilities of the partnership, and the values agreed for the purchase, were:

|  | Book value US\$ | Agreed value US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Premises | 68,400 | 77,600 |
| Equipment | 20,300 | 18,900 |
| Inventory | 12,900 | 11,700 |
| Trade receivables | 8,700 | 8,300 |
| Trade payables (taken over) | 10,900 | 10,900 |
| Bank (not taken over) | 4,350 | not taken |

The purchase consideration is US\$20,300 in cash, 46,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 issued at US\$1.65 each and US\$12,800 of loan notes.

The statement of financial position of Harare Packaging Ltd just before the purchase showed: premises US\$148,000, equipment US\$63,500, inventory US\$37,400, trade receivables US\$26,800 and bank US\$43,300; ordinary share capital US\$158,000 (US\$1 shares), share premium US\$31,000, retained earnings US\$69,500, loan notes US\$26,000 (non-current) and trade payables US\$34,500.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the net assets acquired, at agreed values.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the purchase consideration.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the goodwill.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the journal entries in the books of Harare Packaging Ltd to record the purchase, with narratives.

points.description: Assets debited at agreed values
Goodwill 3,400 debited (own figure)
Trade payables 10,900 and business purchase account 109,000 credited
Second journal: business purchase account debited 109,000
Bank 20,300 and loan notes 12,800 credited
Share capital 46,000 and share premium 29,900 credited

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Journal of Harare Packaging Ltd**

| Date | Details | Debit US\$ | Credit US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 Apr | Premises | 77,600 |  |
|  | Equipment | 18,900 |  |
|  | Inventory | 11,700 |  |
|  | Trade receivables | 8,300 |  |
|  | Goodwill | 3,400 |  |
|  | Trade payables |  | 10,900 |
|  | Business purchase account |  | 109,000 |
|  | *Business of Tanaka and Moyo taken over at agreed values* |  |  |
| 1 Apr | Business purchase account | 109,000 |  |
|  | Bank |  | 20,300 |
|  | Ordinary share capital |  | 46,000 |
|  | Share premium |  | 29,900 |
|  | Loan notes |  | 12,800 |
|  | *Settlement of the purchase consideration* |  |  |

parts.explanation: Journal 1 totals 119,900 each side; journal 2 totals 109,000 each side.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit on realisation in the partnership's books (the bank balance stays with the partners).
parts.explanation: Assets taken over at book value 110,300 less payables 10,900 = 99,400. Profit 109,000 − 99,400 = 9,600 (Tanaka 5,760, Moyo 3,840).
parts.workedSolution: 1. Assets taken over at book value 110,300 less payables 10,900 = 99,400. Profit 109,000 − 99,400 = 9,600 (Tanaka 5,760, Moyo 3,840).

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the gearing ratio of Harare Packaging Ltd after the purchase (non-current liabilities ÷ (issued share capital + all reserves + non-current liabilities) × 100), to one decimal place.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Calculate the current ratio after the purchase as x : 1, to two decimal places.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Evaluate the effect of the purchase on the financial position of Harare Packaging Ltd, using your answers to (f) and (g).

points.description: Gearing rises from 9.1% to 10.4% because loan notes of 12,800 are added, but it remains low
The current ratio falls from 3.12 : 1 to 2.36 : 1 because cash was paid and payables were taken over, but liquidity is still acceptable
Judgement: the financial position is weaker but sound; the benefit depends on the profit earned by the acquired business

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Gearing rises from 9.1% to 10.4% as loan notes of US\$12,800 are added, but remains low. The current ratio falls from 3.12 : 1 to 2.36 : 1 because cash was paid and payables taken over, though liquidity is acceptable. The position is weaker but sound, and the benefit depends on the profit the acquired business earns.

parts.explanation: One mark each for gearing, liquidity and a judgement.

explanation: This FIN25 item combines the purchaser's journals, the vendor's profit on realisation and an analysis of gearing and liquidity.
hints: Value the shares at the issue price.
In (e) the bank balance is not transferred to the realisation account.
Use the formulas printed in the question for gearing.

stem:
Mutare Steel Works makes steel doors. The following information is for the year ended 31 December 2025.

| Item | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Raw materials: inventory at 1 January 2025 | 21,700 |
| Purchases of raw materials | 95,800 |
| Carriage inwards | 2,400 |
| Returns outwards (raw materials) | 1,700 |
| Raw materials: inventory at 31 December 2025 | 23,400 |
| Manufacturing wages | 61,500 |
| Royalties on doors made | 3,700 |
| Indirect factory wages | 14,600 |
| Factory power | 8,950 |
| Depreciation of machinery | 7,450 |
| Rent (60% relates to the factory) | 10,400 |
| Insurance of plant | 2,760 |
| Work in progress at 1 January 2025 | 8,700 |
| Work in progress at 31 December 2025 | 9,700 |
| Sales | 343,500 |
| Finished goods at 1 January 2025 (at transfer price) | 44,200 |
| Finished goods at 31 December 2025 (at transfer price) | 49,400 |
| Selling, distribution and administration expenses | 51,800 |

The factory completed 3,980 doors. Finished goods are transferred to the trading account at cost of production plus 30% (market value). The opening provision for unrealised profit was based on the same mark-up.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the prime cost.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of production.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the manufacturing profit.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the manufacturing account for the year, ending with the value of goods transferred to the trading account.

points.description: Raw materials consumed 94,800 with carriage inwards and returns outwards correctly placed
Direct wages and royalties; prime cost 160,000
Factory overheads listed with the factory share of rent 6,240
Opening work in progress added and closing deducted
Cost of production 199,000
Manufacturing profit 59,700 and value transferred 258,700

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Mutare Steel Works: manufacturing account for the year ended 31 December 2025**

|  | US\$ | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Opening inventory of raw materials |  | 21,700 |
| Purchases of raw materials |  | 95,800 |

| Direct labour (manufacturing wages) |  | 61,500 |

| Total factory overheads |  | 40,000 |
| **Factory cost** |  | 200,000 |
| Add opening work in progress |  | 8,700 |
| Less closing work in progress |  | (9,700) |
| **Cost of production (transferred to the trading account)** |  | 199,000 |

**Mutare Steel Works: extract from the manufacturing account**

|  | US\$ | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cost of production |  | 199,000 |
| Manufacturing profit (30% mark-up on cost of production) |  | 59,700 |
| **Value of goods transferred to the trading account** |  | 258,700 |

parts.explanation: The manufacturing profit is added after the cost of production.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the provision for unrealised profit needed at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the increase in the provision for the year.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Explain what is meant by unrealised profit in closing finished goods.

points.description: The goods are valued at the transfer price, which includes the factory's profit
That profit has not been earned because the goods have not been sold

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Closing finished goods are valued at the transfer price, which includes the factory's profit. The profit is unrealised because the goods have not yet been sold.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: A new supplier offers the same doors at US\$56 each. Evaluate the result for the factory and advise whether the factory should continue to make the doors.

points.description: The cost of production is 50.00 per door, below the supplier's 56, so making is cheaper by 6.00 per door (23,880 for 3,980 doors)
The transfer price of 65.00 is above the new market price of 56, so the manufacturing profit of 59,700 is overstated; at 56 it would be 23,880
Quality, reliability and jobs are non-financial factors
Advice: continue to make the doors, but revise the transfer price to 56 so the results of the factory and the shop are fairly shown

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The factory makes a door for US\$50, which is US\$6 less than the supplier's US\$56, a saving of US\$23,880 over 3,980 doors, so it should continue to manufacture. The transfer price of US\$65 is above the new market price, so the factory profit of US\$59,700 is overstated; at US\$56 it would be US\$23,880. The company should revise the transfer price.

parts.explanation: One mark each for the cost comparison, the overstated profit, non-financial factors and the advice.

explanation: This FIN25 item combines the manufacturing account, manufacturing profit, the provision for unrealised profit and an evaluation of the transfer price.
hints: Carriage inwards is added to purchases.
Provision = closing inventory at transfer price × 30/130.
Only the change in the provision goes through the statement of profit or loss.

stem:
Bulawayo Golf Society keeps only a cash book. At 1 January 2025 its assets were the course and clubhouse US\$124,000, equipment US\$14,900, shop inventory US\$2,430, subscriptions in arrears US\$640 and bank US\$7,150. Its liabilities were subscriptions received in advance US\$360, shop suppliers US\$1,170 and the greenkeepers' wages owing US\$475.

| Receipts for 2025 | US\$ | Payments for 2025 | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Subscriptions | 31,300 | Shop suppliers | 7,690 |
| Shop sales | 11,870 | Greenkeepers' wages | 18,960 |
| Entrance fees | 1,560 | Utilities | 4,230 |
| Competition entry fees | 2,740 | New equipment | 3,150 |
| Grant for new irrigation (specific purpose) | 5,400 | Competition prizes | 1,780 |
| Life membership fees (3 members at 930) | 2,790 | Administration | 2,720 |
| Donations (general) | 990 | Insurance | 1,570 |

At 31 December 2025: subscriptions in arrears US\$780 (after writing off US\$145 as irrecoverable) and in advance US\$415; shop suppliers owed US\$1,360; shop inventory US\$2,710; greenkeepers owed US\$520; insurance prepaid US\$225. Equipment is depreciated at 10% on cost including additions; the course and clubhouse at 1% of the value at the start of the year. Life membership fees are credited to income in equal amounts over 9 years, starting this year. The irrigation grant is held in a separate fund.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated fund at 1 January 2025.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the subscriptions income for the year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Shop:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: calculate the shop purchases

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: calculate the profit on the shop

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate:

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: the greenkeepers' wages expense

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: the total depreciation charge

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the surplus for the year (use the grant as a fund, not as income).

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Prepare the income and expenditure account for the year ended 31 December 2025.

points.description: Subscriptions 31,530, entrance fees 1,560 and donations 990
Profit on the shop 4,270 and on competitions 960 (own figures)
Life membership income 310; the grant is not income
Expenditure: greenkeepers 19,005, insurance 1,345, irrecoverable subscriptions 145 and depreciation 3,045
Totals 39,620 and 30,490 with the surplus

| Donations | 990 |  |

parts.explanation: Capital payments such as equipment are not expenditure.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Calculate the accumulated fund at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Explain how the irrigation grant and the life membership fees are shown in the statement of financial position at 31 December 2025.

points.description: The grant of 5,400 is shown as a separate irrigation fund
The unspent life membership fees of 2,480 are shown as deferred income (a liability)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The grant of US\$5,400 is shown as a separate irrigation fund. The unspent life membership fees of US\$2,480 are shown as deferred income.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Comment on the Society's financial position using the surplus and the accumulated fund.

points.description: The surplus of 9,130 increased the fund by about 6.2%; the Society covered its running costs
Some income (donations, competition profit, life membership) may not recur, so the committee should monitor costs and subscriptions

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The surplus of US\$9,130 raised the fund by about 6.2%, so running costs were covered. Some income such as donations may not recur, so costs and subscriptions should be monitored.

explanation: This FIN25 item prepares a club's accumulated fund, subscriptions, shop profit and income and expenditure account from a cash book and notes.
hints: Convert each cash figure to the amount for the year.
The grant goes to a fund, not to income.
Equipment bought is not an expense.
